processing_steps.method: melting-casting route in an open-air induction furnace (Power Trak 250-10 R Inductotherm)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The developed steel was produced by the conventional melting-casting route in an open-air induction furnace; the as-solidified cast ingot constitutes the cast specimen (state_label 'cast specimen'). No further thermal/mechanical step is applied to this state.

structures.overall_structure: Dual-phase microstructure of delta ferrite (δ) and austenite (γ) in the cast specimen, confirmed by XRD and optical microscopy; the austenite in the cast specimen has a dendritic type structure.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Bruker D8 advanced X-ray diffractometer, Co-Kα (1.79 Å) target
characterization_methods.purpose: To identify the major phases present in the developed steel after casting (and hot forging)
characterization_methods.key_findings: XRD of the cast specimen (Fig. 2a, black pattern) shows the presence of ferrite and austenite; reflections indexed α110, γ111, γ200, α200, γ220, α211, γ311 and γ222 (α: ferrite (δ/α), γ: austenite).

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: specimens prepared by standard metallography + colloidal polishing (0.25 µm) and etched with Villella's Reagent (5 ml HCl + 1 g picric acid + 100 ml ethanol) for 10-15 s
characterization_methods.purpose: To confirm the phases/microstructure of the cast specimen
characterization_methods.key_findings: Optical images (Fig. 2b,c) confirm a dual-phase microstructure in the cast specimen; the austenite in the cast specimen has a dendritic type structure (indicated by blue arrow in Fig. 2b,c).

characterization_methods.purpose: To calculate the volume fraction of phases in the cast specimen
characterization_methods.key_findings: ~26% (volume %) of austenite in the cast sample; unchanged to ~29% in the forged sample, showing only ~3% difference.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Equilibrium phase fractions versus temperature (Fig. 1b); duplex ferrite (δ) + austenite (γ) region measured to be ~650 °C to ~1350 °C; equilibrium transformation sequence L → L+δ → L+δ+γ → γ+δ; BCC phase remains on cooling from liquid (>~1500 °C) to room temperature.
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Used to identify that ferrite present in the cast specimen is δ-ferrite; dilatometry conducted on the forged sample showed no significant transformation-related contraction, consistent with the thermocalc prediction.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Variables include grain size (initial finer austenite grain assumed 40 µm), temperature and alloy composition; interfacial surface energy σ^{γ/ε} taken as 10 mJ/m² (literature range 5-15 mJ/m²).

analytical_models.equation_role: γ_SFE = 2ρΔG^{γ→ε} + 2σ^{γ/ε}, with ΔG^{γ→ε} = ΔG_chem + ΔG_mag + ΔG_ex
analytical_models.model_note: The theoretical SFE of the designed steel is ~35 mJ/m² (within the 20-40 mJ/m² TWIP range). This computation is for the designed alloy (cast is its base state).

unmapped_findings: Measured bulk chemical composition of the developed steel (Table 1, wt.%): Fe bal., Mn 7.79, Al 4.88, Si 0.84, C 0.2, P 0.03, S 0.03; measured by XRF and OES (b0014, b0016).
The designed grade is Fe-8Mn-5Al-0.2C (wt.%) low-density medium Mn steel; the cast specimen is the as-solidified state of this alloy (b0014).
The developed steel shows ~11.35% density reduction compared to conventional steel (~7.8 g/cc), achieved by the addition of ~5 (wt.%) Al and ~1 (wt.%) Si (b0034).
XRD of the cast specimen (Fig. 2a, black 'Cast Specimen' pattern) is indexed with reflections α110, γ111, γ200, α200, γ220, α211, γ311 and γ222; legend 'α: ferrite (δ/α), γ: austenite' (figure_002).
